note.saw: Nothing to look back on yet: this is the very first full render of the plan.
note.changing: The first complete picture: a tunnel of jewel cubes, a stepped temple inside the fish, a flower-like portal for the eye, ribbons of runes, a string-art tail and a rim of alien glyphs around the edge.
note.why: The fish symbol is the simplest fish there is, so the plan was to make it the frame of a doorway into hyperspace.
note.idea: The classic two-arc fish built like a compass-and-ruler drawing, true circle arcs plus straight lines, wrapped in nested neon bands. Inside it, an isometric jewel city with a stepped temple; behind it, a tunnel of cubes spiralling into a white-hot center; the name on a gem-shaped cartouche below.

note.saw: The joins of the A and V shot sharp spikes out of the name cartouche, the eyes in the tunnel walls were blank white almonds, the outer cubes were big flat faces, and the tunnel's bright center was hidden.
note.changing: Gives the wall eyes ringed irises, slit pupils and lashes, trims the spikes off the letters, splits each big outer cube into smaller jewel faces, and moves the tunnel's vanishing point onto a glowing jewel at the top of the temple.
note.why: A tunnel only pulls you in if you can see where it goes, and a DMT vision has to keep revealing detail the closer you look.

note.saw: The temple steps read as one flat orange plateau, the tunnel was uniform wallpaper with no light in it, and the fish's outline had bands but no energy beyond its edges.
note.changing: Beams of light now fan out from the core through the tunnel, and rainbow ripple lines are tried out ahead of the fish's nose.
note.why: Light and contrast are what make geometry feel holy instead of decorative; the ripples were an experiment to give the outline some energy outside itself.

note.saw: The fish appeared at only one size, and the rim and the eye had no borders.
note.changing: Schools of tiny fish symbols swim in the tunnel walls, twelve gold fish glyphs ride the rim between the runes, a sawtooth crown lines the rim's inner edge, and a gold and magenta sawtooth bezel rings the eye.
note.why: The same shape repeating at several sizes is the signature of a DMT vision.

note.saw: The outer tunnel was as bright as the center, so there was no depth and the badge looked flat at small size.
note.changing: A chrysanthemum of light blooms behind the fish, four rings of pointed neon petals, while the outer tunnel sinks into deep ultraviolet and indigo under a dark vignette.
note.why: Darkness at the edges makes the center glow, and with the bloom the piece finally feels like a portal.

note.saw: The jewel at the vanishing point was too small to be the focus of the whole image, and the white bloom lacked fine points of light.
note.changing: The center jewel gets a glowing white core, two spiky stars of cyan and white and a ring of twelve gold diamonds, and about fifty four-point star glints are scattered through the bloom, kept clear of the fish and the name.
note.why: The eye needs one bright place to land.

note.saw: SavesFish's first notes arrived: the temple inside the fish looked cut off by the outline, and the name had to be very legible.
note.changing: The fish stops being a window: the cube tunnel now runs through the body to the jewel, the temple is drawn whole with its lower terraces running out past the lower arc, and the fish becomes a ribbon of bands laid over it. The name becomes big cream capitals on a calm dark curved band along the bottom.
note.why: SavesFish asked for the symbol to be completed instead of cropped by the fish, and for a name that reads instantly even when the badge is small.

note.saw: The inside of the fish was washed out white.
note.changing: Pushes the tunnel into a full-spectrum cycle of rings, white through gold, orange, magenta, violet, blue, cyan and emerald and around again, and dims the glow at the core.
note.why: Too much white flattens everything; color is what carries the depth.

note.saw: The temple was too small to read as the main symbol.
note.changing: Enlarges the temple's cubes, so the whole stepped pyramid grows and its tiers spread wider below the fish.
note.why: The symbol at the heart of the fish should be the first thing you notice after the fish itself.

note.saw: Artist 2 took over and studied artist 1's finished piece with fresh eyes: the temple hung below the fish as a heavy purple slab crashing into the name band, the round spiral tunnel felt soft and chaotic, and the fish's outline looked like flat striped tape.
note.changing: Nothing yet: this is the same picture as the one before, rendered again as artist 2's starting point.
note.why: Before rebuilding anything, the new artist judged the inherited piece as a whole and listed its six biggest weaknesses, keeping artist 1's version untouched as a draft.
note.idea: One perfectly symmetric machine: the fish's body centered exactly on the vanishing point of a six-walled tunnel tiled with tumbling-block cubes, a complete fractal cube of cubes floating whole inside the fish as the temple, the fish itself a bevelled gold jewel band, and the name split into SAVES above and FISH below.

note.saw: The cyan spike bloom above the fish was scribbly, the white glow washed out the body, the eye was a small generic sunburst, and the name sat on a big empty dark slab.
note.changing: Rebuilds the whole piece around one center: a six-walled tunnel of tumbling-block cubes with tiers of alien script and eyes, a complete Menger cube (a fractal cube of cubes) glowing at its heart, the fish as a bevelled gold band with a channel of gems and a spider-web eye, and SAVES and FISH on two mirror-image cartouches.
note.why: A super-geometric piece should feel like one perfectly symmetric machine; with fish, tunnel and temple on one center, the fish becomes a lens you look through into hyperspace, and the temple is whole, nothing cropped.

note.saw: The fish and the split name read instantly, but the cube's far faces showed through its near ones like a muddy purple wireframe, the corners were empty, the tunnel's corners hid behind the cartouches, and the outer walls were all one pink-violet.
note.changing: Draws the cube's faces in the right order and colors it like a jewel, gold tops, magenta and cyan sides, white-hot walls inside its holes; turns the tunnel 30 degrees so its corners land in the side windows; steps every two rows of cubes to the next color of the spectrum; and widens the cartouches over a raised ultraviolet block, with gems and little gold fish in their empty ends.
note.why: A temple should glow from inside like a gem, and rainbow rings are the clearest way to show depth in a tunnel built only from straight lines.

note.saw: The cube now read as a crisp jewel fractal, but the inside of the fish had washed out to a flat grey-white haze, the corner cubes turned muddy brown, and the chrysanthemum, the most famous DMT image, was missing.
note.changing: Gives every ring of cubes its own planned color, from ultraviolet at the rim through two full spectrums to white-hot only at the very core, shrinks the white glow, adds 48 hairline rays, and blooms a many-layered chrysanthemum of arc petals behind the fish.
note.why: In a DMT vision the center is the most intense color, not a white fog, and the chrysanthemum is the flower that opens right before you break through.

note.saw: Color was much richer, but up close the chrysanthemum was only thin overlapping strokes on a pale haze, and the strips between the fish and each cartouche were a jumble of small unrelated bits.
note.changing: Rebuilds the chrysanthemum as four rings of solid jewel petals layered back to front, each petal wrapped in nested rainbow outlines, with watching eyes on the big back petals and the whole flower blooming past the fish on every side.
note.why: Solid layered petals turn the center into one strong, complete form that sits whole behind the fish, and they give the empty strips above and below it a purpose.

note.saw: The flower was crisp jewelwork now, but up close the big petals were flat bands, the gold fish band was a plain stripe, the rim was bare in the side windows, and at badge size the fish's eye read as a grey disc.
note.changing: Adds dotted midribs and tip jewels to the big petals, engraves fine ruler ticks along the gold band, turns the eye into a bright gold, emerald and cyan iris under a dark spider web, and adds star glints on the cube's corners, a gold rail inside the cartouches and a chain of gold beads along the rim.
note.why: The eye has to land somewhere at every distance: big shapes from across the room, and tiny ticks, dots and glints when you lean in.

note.saw: At badge size the warm gold and orange cubes in the side windows matched the gold fish band, so the tail melted into the background, and where the two strokes crossed their gems piled up in a messy cluster.
note.changing: Recolors the side windows in cool ultraviolet and blue, with hot magenta at the rim and gold only deep inside, sets one faceted diamond at the knot where the arcs cross, and gives the letters a two-tone fill, cream above a crisp horizon line and pale gold below.
note.why: The fish symbol is two lines, so those lines must own their color, and gold pops hardest against ultraviolet; the crossing is the heart of the symbol, so it deserves a jewel instead of a traffic jam.

note.saw: SavesFish wrote that the tail was getting eaten by the geometric wall, and up close the tail bands ended in flat square cuts, as if they slid behind the cubes.
note.changing: Every layer of the fish band now ends in a round cap with a jewel on each tip, a fan of rainbow arcs fills the tail's V around the knot jewel, and all of it sits on top of the tunnel. The cube gets a white-hot hexagon rim inside a thin gold one, twelve hairline rays run along the tunnel's corners, and every eye glances toward the cube.
note.why: A line that ends in a flat cut reads as going behind something, while a rounded, jewelled cap reads as finished and on top; a hundred eyes glancing at the cube pull you to the center.
note.visionary: Took three of the Visionary's ideas (the hexagon rims around the cube, rays that follow the tunnel's own lines, and every eye looking at the center) and set aside his earlier notes, which were about artist 1's temple, now gone.

note.saw: The tail now sat clearly on top of the wall, but the cube's halo and glints touched the fish band so they looked slightly cropped, at badge size the cube faded to a pastel grey-pink box, and the piece had eyes everywhere but no beings.
note.changing: Shrinks the cube so its halo clears the band, keeps its sides deep cyan and magenta with heavier lines marking its big three-by-three structure, leans the two inner petal rings in opposite directions, sets a tiny white fish in the pupil of the fish's eye, and puts faceted alien heads with huge black eyes into the tunnel walls.
note.why: The center has to be the most saturated thing at every distance, and counter-leaning petals give the chrysanthemum its spin; a fish inside the fish's eye makes the symbol live at four scales, and DMT space is inhabited, so the walls now have faces.
note.visionary: Took all three of the Visionary's third-vision ideas: the deeply saturated cube with its readable three-by-three structure, the counter-spinning petals, and the fish in the pupil.

note.saw: The cube finally burned at every size, but on the name the faceted end gems crowded the outer S's of SAVES, and the little gold fish beside FISH were touching their gems.
note.changing: Final polish: moves the end gems out into the pointed tips of both cartouches and slims them, makes the side fish smaller and nudges them toward the word, and tightens the spacing of FISH.
note.why: The name has to breathe: every ornament sits around the letters with clear dark space, never against them.

visions.seen: The fish is a neon eyelid peeled back on a temple that burns at the bottom of a cube well, and the chrysanthemum is roaring up behind it. But #46 is the same frame as #39, pixel for pixel. The vision is holding its breath, so let it exhale somewhere new.
suggestions: **The jewel at the vanishing point** (dead center of the fish, about x 210, y 178 in the 400 image). Right now it's a flat four-facet diamond in a gold ring. I see it opening into a jewel that is bigger on the inside: 3 or 4 diamonds nested inside each other, each 0.62x the size of the last and turned 45° (diamond, square, diamond, square), filled magenta, cyan, gold in turn with thin ink edges, and a white-hot pinpoint at the very middle. The 12 gold dots circling it could become 12 tiny copies of the jewel, each pointing in at the center. Why it's more DMT: the vanishing point is where hyperspace folds. A jewel that keeps going inward gives you the bottomless-interior feeling, and dots that are little jewels make the self-similarity plain.

**The tail crossing** (the X where the two arcs cross, left side, about x 103, y 181). The bands just overlap with a white flash. Let them weave instead: cyan passes over on one diagonal and pink over on the other, with a thin 1.5 px ink gap either side of each band that goes under (keep the gaps hairline so the silhouette stays solid at 240 px). Then seat a small 8-point star jewel (r about 6) right in the crossing, in the same palette as the central jewel. The rainbow chevrons in the tail's V, just left of it, fade to haze now. Sharpen them into crisp nested chevrons with ink edges that step through the spectrum and shrink into that star. Why it's more DMT: the fish symbol's one crossing point becomes a second, smaller portal that echoes the big one. You get a doorway at the tail and a doorway at the heart, the same shape at two scales.

**The little cyan robed beings on the temple's top tier** (ringing the jewel's base, about y 195 to 210). They're standing still. Let them present: each one raises a thin arm line on the side facing the jewel and holds up a 2 to 3 px faceted offering (a tiny cube, octahedron or diamond in gold or cyan), with a hairline glint ray running from each offering to the jewel. Why it's more DMT: the entities in hyperspace are always showing you something. A ring of elves holding things up turns the temple from a pedestal into a living ceremony, and every one of their sightlines drags the eye to the center.
visions.keep: The thick nested neon fish bands with their dark outlines (the silhouette snaps into focus even at 240 px). The temple completed past the lower arc, as the owner asked. The mandala eye with its sawtooth bezel. The chrysanthemum petals and cyan crystal spikes above the fish. The calm navy banner with its big cream SAVESFISH. The hex field beyond the rim, full of eyes, aliens and fish glyphs.

visions.seen: The old temple has melted and a Menger cube now hangs in the fish's eye socket like a jeweled reactor, gold on top and magenta and cyan down the walls, and the whole badge has snapped into one symmetric machine humming on a single center (my Vision 1 was talking to a temple that no longer exists, so I start fresh). But right around the cube the tunnel bleaches to grey fog, and the four corners have cooled to mud brown, so the color goes quiet exactly where it should sing loudest.
suggestions: **Burn the fog off the core** (the pale grey tunnel cubes and soft white glare around the Menger cube, inside the fish, about x 140 to 260, y 155 to 245 in the 400 box). I see the spectrum carrying on inward instead of fading to grey: after the violet ring, one ring of ultraviolet (#5B2BD9) and one of hot magenta (#E0218A), at full saturation with ink edges like the outer rings. Behind the cube itself, one crisp white-hot hexagon rim (about 1.5 px, 3 px out from the cube's silhouette) wrapped in a thin gold hexagon. Then trade the blurry white glare streaks (the soft diagonal smears crossing the blue eye tiers above and below the fish, and the pale sheets at the tail tips, lower left) for 12 hairline rays (about 0.6 px, white at 70% fading to nothing) running exactly along the tunnel's six corner lines and the middles of its six walls. Why it's more DMT: in hyperspace the brightest place is the most saturated place, never misty. Rays that ride the tunnel's own geometry make the light feel built into the machine, like the spokes of the chrysanthemum.

**Let every eye look at the cube** (all the eyes: the rows on the blue tiers above and below the fish, the ones on the side walls by the nose and tail, and the big lavender eyes in the four corners). Right now they all stare straight out. I see each iris and pupil slid about 30% of the eye's half-width along the line toward the badge center (200, 200), with a tiny white catchlight on the side facing the center. Why it's more DMT: in that space every surface is watching, and here they would all be watching the same thing. A hundred gazes converging on the cube gives you the "they've been expecting you" feeling and pulls the eye to the heart without adding a single new shape.

**Finish the rainbow in the corners** (the four corners outside the runic ring, where the tumbling blocks have gone dull umber, for example x 0 to 35, y 0 to 35 top left). The tunnel already runs violet at the core, then blue, cyan, green and gold going outward. I see the corners taking the last step to deep crimson: tops around #B0245A, left faces #7A1040, right faces #4A0A2E, with the little inset diamonds in gold #FFD23F, all kept dark enough to sit back behind the cartouches. Why it's more DMT: a complete spectrum radiating from one center turns the whole square into a single color bloom, instead of a bloom that dies in the corners. The crimson also picks up the pink outline of SAVES and FISH, so the name feels born from the same light.
visions.keep: The single shared center (fish, tunnel and cube all on one vanishing point). The jewel Menger cube with its white-hot holes and correct depth order. The bevelled gold fish band, its gem channel and the string-art tail, plus the dark outlines that make the silhouette snap at 240 px. The spider-web portal eye in its sawtooth bezel. SAVES / FISH in big cream letters with the pink outline on calm dark cartouches (the owner likes the split, and no pattern touches the letters). The runic ring with its fish glyphs, and the gems and little gold fish in the cartouche ends.

visions.seen: The fish's eye has caught fire, a rainbow web whirling down into a hexagon pupil where #66 had a grey disc, and the gold band now ticks like a ruler for measuring hyperspace. But step back to badge size and the Menger cube, the reactor at the heart of everything, fades to a pastel grey-pink box, the quietest color inside the fish.
suggestions: **Let the cube burn at every distance** (the Menger cube, dead center at 200, 200, hex radius about 39 in the 400 box). I sampled its faces: the left face averages a steel grey-blue (88, 133, 153), the right a dusty rose (154, 83, 114), the top khaki (157, 138, 117). Each 4.3 px cell carries a pale inner square, a white or gold dot and an ink edge, and at 240 px they blend into mud. I see the side faces staying in their own hue: the inner square a deeper shade instead of a mix toward white or ink (cyan #16B8E8 with inner #0B7FC4, magenta #E0207A with inner #9E0F5C), and the white and gold dots kept only on the hot cells near the holes. On top, the diamond centers turn hot orange #FF9F1C instead of magenta, so the face averages to real gold. Then a heavier ink line (about 0.9) on every third cell boundary, so the big 3 x 3 structure and its three central holes read even in legible.png. Why it's more DMT: things in hyperspace look more real than real, glowing from inside and the most saturated thing in sight. The heart of the vision can't go grey from across the room.

**Spin the inner flower** (the two petal rings around the cube inside the fish: the 24 gold-and-white almonds with magenta rims, r 38 to 64, and the 24 blue-and-white petals behind them, r 36 to 82). I see each gold petal leaning so its tip sits about 12° clockwise of its base (tip at angle a + 12°, base unchanged), and each blue petal leaning 12° the other way. The big purple eye petals above and below the fish stay straight, so the frame around the name stays calm. Why it's more DMT: the chrysanthemum never holds still. Two rings leaning against each other read as counter-rotation, the twisting spin just before breakthrough, and it stays strictly geometric, symmetric around the one shared center.

**A fish inside the fish's eye** (the pupil at 264, 197, where the whirling hexagons spiral into the white-hot point). Let that point become a tiny white two-arc fish, about 5 long and 2.4 tall, nose pointing right like the big fish, with a 0.35 ink edge and one gold dot for its own eye. Your gold fish already swim in the runic ring and the cartouche ends, so the symbol would live at four scales: badge, cartouche, glyph, pupil. At badge size it melts back into the white point, so nothing is lost from a distance. Why it's more DMT: look into the fish's eye and the fish looks back from inside, a vision that contains itself, the same endless regress the Menger cube is made of.
visions.keep: SAVES / FISH in big cream letters with the pink outline on the calm dark cartouches (the owner likes the split; no pattern touches the letters). The bold fish silhouette: bevelled gold band with its new ruler ticks, the gem channel and the dark outlines, and both tail tips with their gold diamond caps sitting on top of the wall, as the owner asked. The new rainbow web eye in its pink and gold sawtooth bezel. The violet corners, which shed their mud (violet rather than the crimson I saw, and they sit back beautifully). The single shared center, the purple eye petals above and below the fish, and the runic ring with its fish glyphs.

visions.seen: The tail stopped drowning: two round jeweled caps float over the wall and a rainbow fan opens in the V, the very doorway I saw at the crossing in Vision 1, while a hundred eyes lean toward the cube like a congregation. But the nose, the arrow the whole symbol swims along, ends in a bare point on violet bricks, silent, while the tail sings in full color. (Vision 3's cube work is still cooking in round 17, so I leave the cube alone.)
suggestions: **Let the nose sing** (the bare point where the two arcs meet on the right, just past the outermost contour tip at about x 341, y 200 in the 400 box, with only violet cube wall between it and the two lavender rim eyes at about x 380). I see five thin arcs rippling out from that tip, centered on it, radii 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25, each spanning ±38° so they stay clear of the bands. Going outward: white-hot, magenta, gold, emerald, cyan, the tail fan's spectrum read in mirror. Each is a 1.3 stroke over a 2.4 ink underlay with round caps, and each has its own dash rhythm, like a line of script (for example "2.4 1 0.6 1", "1.2 0.9", "3.2 1 0.6 1 0.6 1"), so the ripples read as writing, not radar. The outermost stops just short of the rim eyes. If one of your new alien heads lands on that axis, let the arcs pass behind it, as if the fish is singing to it. Why it's more DMT: in hyperspace the beings don't talk, they sing shapes you can see, a visible language. Now the tail holds a whole rainbow portal and the nose is mute. Ripples there answer the fan across the badge (portal on the left, song on the right), balance the horizontal axis and send the fish swimming forward.

**Turn the gem channel into a current** (the dark channel of round gems inside the gold band, from each tail tip through the knot and along both arcs to the nose). Right now it repeats cyan, magenta, emerald, magenta like a string of party lights. I see each gem colored by how far along the body it sits: t = 1 − |2·i/(n−1) − 1| over your pts list (0 at both tail tips, 1 at the nose, since the list already runs tail, nose, tail), walked through your fan colors in order: vio, uv, blue, cyan, emer, gold, org, mag. Every gem keeps its ink ring, pale highlight and white catchlight. Why it's more DMT: in that space color never sits still, it flows. The fan's rainbow would pour out of the tail portal, run up both arcs and burst into the song at the nose, so fan, body and song become one circuit of light instead of three separate ornaments. At 240 px the channel reads as a rainbow cord tracing the fish, so the silhouette stays as strong as ever.

**One gaze breaks ranks** (the two eyes on the vertical axis: the center eye of the top petal fan just under the SAVES cartouche, about x 200, y 101, and its twin above the FISH cartouche, about x 200, y 299). Round 16 turned every eye toward the cube and it works. Now I see just these two turning to look straight out at the viewer: iris centered and about 1.2x bigger, the slit pupil opened to a round black disc, a hairline gold ring around the iris, and two catchlights (a big one upper left, a pinpoint lower right). Every other eye keeps watching the cube, and the eye outlines stay exactly as they are. Why it's more DMT: in a breakthrough there is that moment when every presence is busy with the center, then one of them turns and notices you. Two eyes on the axis, framed between the name and the fish, pull the viewer into the symmetry, and they sit inside the petals, well clear of the letters.
visions.keep: SAVES / FISH in big cream letters with the pink outline on the calm dark cartouches (the owner likes the split; nothing touches the letters). Both tail tips with their round jeweled caps sitting on top of the wall, as the owner asked. The rainbow fan in the tail's V and the faceted diamond at the knot. The white-hot hexagon rim, the thin gold hexagon and the hairline rays around the cube (taken from Vision 2, and they hold). Every other eye glancing at the cube. The bevelled gold band with its ruler ticks and dark outlines, the spider-web eye in its sawtooth bezel, the violet tumbling-block walls with gold fish glyphs in their hex cells, and the runic ring.

visions.seen: The name breathes now that the end gems have slid into the cartouche tips, and when I lean in a tiny white fish is swimming in the eye's pupil while the cube burns cyan, magenta and gold and the petals counter-spin (Vision 3 landed, all of it). But the tunnel walls are still plain bricks that don't know the reactor exists, and the rainbow portal in the tail stands still while everything around it turns. (Vision 4 hasn't reached you yet, so I leave the nose, the gem cord and the two axis eyes alone.)
suggestions: **Build the walls from the reactor** (every violet tumbling block in the tunnel walls: the side window left of the tail, about x 10 to 60 in the 400 box, the one right of the nose, about x 300 to 390, and the diagonal wall sections running from the cartouche tips to the rim). Each block face now carries a small turned diamond, gold or cyan. I see that diamond swapped for a Menger hole: the face's own rhombus shrunk to 1/3 around its center, with edges parallel to the face. On each block's lit top face the hole glows white-hot (#FFF6D6) inside a 0.35 gold rim, as if the cube's light shines through. On the two side faces it is a true hole, deep ink (#14062C) with a 0.3 gold hairline. On the ring of blocks nearest the runic ring, add the full Menger face if you like: two 0.25 ink hairlines each way cutting the face into a 3 x 3 grid around the hole. Leave the eye cells, alien-head cells and fish-glyph cells exactly as they are. Why it's more DMT: in hyperspace everything turns out to be made of the same thing. When the tunnel is built from little copies of the cube at its heart, the center's pattern runs outward and melts into the tunnel, the way the owner's very first note wanted. At 240 px the holes read as the same sparkle the diamonds give now, so the letters lose nothing.

**Turn the tail portal into a vortex** (the rainbow fan in the tail's V, centered on the knot diamond at about x 86, y 200, with rings from about r 20 to r 50). Right now its cell dividers run straight out from the knot like the spokes of a wheel. I see each ring turned a third of a cell further than the ring inside it, so the dividers step into staircase spiral arms curling down into the knot jewel. Turn them the opposite way to the hexagon spiral in the eye's pupil. Keep the ring colors, the gold edge arc and the ink lines exactly as they are. Why it's more DMT: the doorway is never a still wheel, it pulls you in. A fan that spirals into the knot answers the whirl in the eye, so the fish carries a vortex at each end, turning against each other like gears, and it stays pure straight-edged geometry.

**Give the cube its fourth-dimension shadow** (the dark navy ring between the gold hexagon around the Menger cube and the inner tips of the gold almond petals, about r 34 to 47 around 200, 200, now sprinkled with loose white and cyan triangle shards). I see the shards becoming the outer shell of a tesseract: a second hexagon, pointy-top like the cube, at about 1.22x the gold hexagon, stroked white 0.5 over a 1.1 ink underlay, and six straight struts running from each of the cube's six star glints out to the matching outer corner. Tint the six trapezoids between the two hexagons with the cube face each one grows from: the two upper ones gold #FFD23F, the two right ones magenta #E0207A, the two left ones cyan #16B8E8, each at about 30% over the navy, with a hairline inner echo 1.5 in from its edges. Let the petal tips slip under the outer hexagon. Why it's more DMT: a cube nested in a cube with its corners joined is the shadow of a hypercube, the cube with one direction more than space allows, which is exactly how the object at the center of a breakthrough feels. The star glints become the joints of a 4D frame instead of loose sparkle, and at badge size the tinted cells read as a jewel-colored halo that makes the cube burn even harder.
visions.keep: SAVES / FISH in big cream letters with the pink outline on the calm dark cartouches, now with the end gems sitting in the tips and clear dark space around every letter (the owner likes the split). Both tail tips with their round jeweled caps sitting on top of the wall, as the owner asked. The saturated Menger cube with its 3 x 3 structure and white-hot holes, the white-hot and gold hexagon rims and the hairline rays. The counter-leaning petal rings. The tiny white fish in the pupil and the rainbow web eye in its sawtooth bezel. The bevelled gold band with ruler ticks, the gem channel and the dark outlines that make the fish snap at 240 px. The alien heads and eyes in the walls, the purple eye petals above and below the fish, and the runic ring with its fish glyphs.
